To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the mutual exclusivity-based methods have been successfully applied to various cancer types, (ii) the mutual exclusivities of genes and pathways are highly context dependent, and (iii) the mutual exclusiveness of genes and pathways can be used as a powerful tool to infer cancer driver pathways or modules.

(1) we have developed a new computational model, the mutual exclusivity network model, to discover driver pathways or modules from cancer genomic data and (2) the new model has been applied to the analysis of cancer genomics datasets, including breast, colorectal, glioblastoma, lung, melanoma, ovarian and prostate cancers, and the results have shown that the new model is effective and can be used for cancer pathway/module discovery
(1) we have developed a computational model and algorithm for discovering driver gene pathways in cancer with the mutual exclusivity constraint.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How to define driver pathway? What is the relationship between driver pathway and mutual exclusivity? How to discover driver pathways with mutual exclusivity property? How to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutual exclusivity is not sufficient but necessary for a gene set to be a driver pathway.
, although the mutual exclusivity-based methods have achieved great success in identifying driver pathways in cancer, the current methods still face several challenges and limitations.
there is no best algorithm for discovering driver pathways in cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutual exclusivity property of driver genes/pathways has been well utilized in the literature and the existing algorithms have achieved promising results in various cancer datasets.
the discovery of driver pathways in cancer is a challenging task, but it can be achieved by using a combination of computational models and high-throughput sequencing data.

, in the past decade, the development of computational models for discovering driver pathways has been mainly driven by two major factors: (1) the development of high-through-put sequencing technologies, (2) the availability of cancer genomics and other omics data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of new computational methods for cancer genomics data analysis is an active research area with a lot of opportunities and challenges.
the problem of discovering driver pathways is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem.
the development of computational models is still in its infancy.
